summary: Qilin (formerly Agenda) is a Russian-speaking RaaS that became the most prolific ransomware operation in 2025, publishing 40+ victims a month. Affiliates typically log in through VPNs lacking MFA using leaked credentials or exploit edge devices, then establish multiple RMM tools, kill EDR via vulnerable drivers and harvest credentials at scale (including a domain-wide Chrome password theft via a logon GPO). Data is staged with WinRAR and exfiltrated with Cyberduck to cloud storage before deploying both Windows and Linux/ESXi encryptors, including running the Linux ELF encryptor on Windows hosts through remote-management tooling and WSL.
uniqueTraits: Domain-wide Chrome credential harvesting via a logon GPO (IPScanner.ps1 / logon.bat staged in SYSVOL)
Linux ELF encryptor executed on Windows hosts (WinSCP transfer, Splashtop/WSL execution) to evade Windows-centric EDR
BYOVD EDR killing (eskle.sys) plus dark-kill / HRSword
Cyberduck multipart uploads to Backblaze for exfiltration
Two-encryptor deployment: one PsExec-propagated, one encrypting network shares from a single host

chain.procedure: Logs in to VPN gateways without MFA using leaked or purchased administrator credentials; dwell of ~2.5 weeks before hands-on activity in the Sophos case.
chain.noAtomicReason: Logon with stolen VPN/remote-access credentials has no local atomic; validate with VPN/IdP authentication telemetry (no MFA, unusual geo/ASN).

chain.procedure: Exploitation of edge and enterprise application vulnerabilities (e.g. SAP NetWeaver CVE-2025-31324 reported in 2025-26 activity).
chain.noAtomicReason: Exploitation of an internet-facing service is not reproducible with a local Windows atomic; validate with perimeter/WAF and application logs instead.
